text:
maria: Quick heads-up — onboarding run for customer 'Nectar' LoRA adapter finished (quick eval pack). Seeing two classes of oddities: tokenizer shifts for currency/date tokens and a small but consistent drop on invoice-extraction F1 after INT4 quant. Putting raw smoke notes here for triage.

sasha: can you paste the failing examples and the exact command you ran? especially the quant flags.

maria: pasted below. run context: dedicated cluster (g5-8x), runtime v2.3.1, base model = redwood/longplay-7B, adapter = nectar-lora-v1.2. Quant test run: --quant=int4 --fallback-fp16=false --kv-cache=on

maria: ```bash
# quick smoke command
run_eval --model redwood/longplay-7B:nector-lora-v1.2 --prompts tests/nectar/smoke_prompts.json --quant int4 --runtime v2.3.1 --out /tmp/nr_eval.json
```

maria: short excerpt of /tmp/nr_eval.json (token alignments trimmed):
```
prompt: "Total due: $1,234.56 on 2025-02-03"
gold:  "{\"amount\":\"1234.56\", \"date\":\"2025-02-03\"}"
int4_out: "{\"amount\":\"1234.00\", \"date\":\"2025-02-??\"}"
notes: amount rounding to 2-decimal but decimals truncated in some cases, date tokenized as three tokens -> parser fails on last token.
```

jin: interesting — is this a tokenizer vocabulary shift (adapter introduced new embeddings) or a decoder probability mass change due to quant noise? can you share top-k logits for the problematic token?

maria: grabbed logits for the last date token on a failing example:
```json
{"top3": [["03", 0.42], ["02", 0.19], ["??", 0.08]]}
```
(weird that "03" prob dropped compared to fp16 run where top was "03" 0.71)

eval-bot: quick-stats from smoke pack (n=120 prompts) -> overall exact-match 86.7% (fp16 baseline 89.2%), invoice-F1 delta: -0.075, tokenizer-mismatch rate: 6/120. Full artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/nr/eval/4167890123/

devon: thanks. can we repro locally with tokens printed? if tokenizer-mismatch is the issue, a token remap or patch in tokenizer config may fix it quickly. otherwise fallback path = pin to fp16 for Nectar in production until we patch.

sasha: @maria any custom special tokens in Nectar adapter (e.g., currency-symbol normalization)? sometimes merges accidentally override tokenizer pre-tokenization rules.

maria: no explicit special tokens added by Nectar team; adapter only modifies attention and MLP weights (LoRA). I ran tokenizer-diff tool and saw offset mapping for "$" around some indices. attaching diff snippet.

maria: ```
# tokenizer-diff snippet
- base token id 523 -> "$"
+ merged token id 523 -> "$", but now ties to subtoken 1243 for numeric sequences
```

jin: that suggests adapter changed embedding matrix alignment after merge step (embedding IDs preserved but weight updates pushed some mass? odd for LoRA). Could be a serialization mismatch in the adapter apply script. Which apply script version?

maria: apply script: scripts/apply_lora.py @ commit 3f4b2e (from onboarding repo). I used `--merge-mode=overlay`.

jin: try re-applying with `--merge-mode=remap` (the safer path that re-assigns token indices) and rerun the smoke. Also compare raw embedding norms before/after.

sasha: agree. also recommend adding a small prompt-level patch: if tokenizer-mismatch detected, run numeric/date normalizer pre-tokenize as a temporary mitigation.

maria: plan: 1) reapply with remap + compute embedding norms (run now) 2) rerun smoke with int4 + fp16 baseline 3) if mismatch persists, push a quick tokenizer remap to customer branch and hold int4 rollout. will post results in ~30m.

eval-bot: kickoff: embedding-norm-job queued (job id ej-4167890200).

devon: if you need a quick rollback toggle for Nectar on dedicated, I can stage a config flag so traffic stays on fp16 until we flip.

maria: thanks — doing step 1 now. small update in 10.

maria: update 10m later: re-applied with remap, embedding norms show a 0.6% shift (was 1.8% with overlay). reran smoke pack: exact-match 88.9%, invoice-F1 delta -0.015 vs fp16, tokenizer-mismatch 1/120 (down from 6). logs: s3://redwood-ci/nr/eval/4167890123/round2/

sasha: excellent improvement. next: can we get a 1hr soak on a subset of Nectar's real prompts and monitor false-positive invoice extractions? I'll craft a 500-prompt subset.

jin: also run with kv-cache off for a quick check — sometimes caching + int4 rounding interacts with incremental decoding.

maria: adding kv-cache=false run to soak. thanks all. final suggestion for rollout doc: prefer remap apply-mode for customer adapters that touch tokenizer-adjacent layers; overlay only for pure attention-only patches. I'll draft short onboarding note. :memo:

devon: when you have the soak pass, ping me and I'll flip the rollout toggle to int4 for canary traffic (10% traffic) else keep fp16.

maria: will do. closing comments here once soak finishes. thanks! :thumbsup:
